subject.title: fix: guarded fetch falls back to IPv6 when IPv4 is unreachable

question: Should guarded fetch deliberately provide all SSRF-validated IPv4 and IPv6 candidates to Node’s Happy-Eyeballs path, while retaining IPv4-first behavior for ordinary single-address lookups?
rationale: The patch does not broaden the validated address set, but it changes which validated addresses Node may attempt at runtime inside the SSRF guard; that policy boundary needs explicit owner acceptance.

options.title: Accept the validated dual-stack path
options.body: Confirm that `{ all: true }` may expose every already validated pinned address to Node family autoselection and proceed with the existing narrow patch.

options.title: Keep IPv4-only automatic behavior
options.body: Retain the current single-family behavior and pursue a different owner-approved fallback design, leaving the linked timeout unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Accept the validated dual-stack path
recommendation.body: Confirm that `{ all: true }` may expose every already validated pinned address to Node family autoselection and proceed with the existing narrow patch.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level guarded-network policy choice rather than a contributor follow-up.
